modalLead: The figures on a custom widget can be sized and drawn as bars, the shortcut letters can stay out of the way until you need them, and a search that finds nothing now points at the bookmarks it did not look through.

items.text: Every figure on a custom widget can have its own size. A tile whose numbers were all drawn the same size left you to work out which one mattered. Each figure is now Normal, Large, Small or a Bar — so the number you built the tile for can lead, and the ones giving it context can sit quietly underneath. The bar is offered on a percentage, where a share of a whole is something it can actually draw, and it takes its colour from the theme you are using.

A response time reads as whole milliseconds. The AdGuard tile showed its average processing time as 0.0051589999999999995 under a label reading “avg ms”. It now reads 5. Any service that answers in seconds can use the new Milliseconds format and say so; a widget already on a page keeps the format it was saved with, and the dropdown is where that changes.
A figure on a custom widget can be edited again. Opening one for editing left the form empty, so the only way to correct a figure was to delete it and add it back.
The figures down a widget's rows line up. Each row measured its own numbers, so a column of them sat at a different distance from the edge on every line.

The shortcut letters are on. Every dashboard shows them again, including the ones where they had been switched off — they are the reminder of what your own shortcuts are, and that is worth the width. If you would rather not have them, Config → Appearance has three answers now: always, only on the row you are on, or never; and once you have chosen, that choice stays.

The shortcut letters can appear only on the row you are on. With them on, the letters sat in a column of their own down the right of every category — as loud as the bookmark names beside them, and holding the width that made those names truncate. With them off, you lost the reminder of what your own shortcuts are. There is now a third answer: On the row I am on. The letter floats in over the end of the name while your pointer or keyboard selection is on that row, nothing moves when it appears, and the names get about five characters of width back. A new install still shows the letters always; this is the setting to reach for when the column is in the way. Under Config → Appearance.
The floating button bar no longer lets the page read through it. Bookmark rows scrolling underneath showed through the bar, so the icons sat on moving text.

The search mode has a key, and sits where you would look for it. Whether typing letters finds a bookmark's name or its shortcut is now under Config → Behavior → Search, called Switch Search Mode. It used to be a tickbox under Appearance → Layout labelled “Interleave categories across columns”, which is not what it does — ticking it to rearrange your columns changed how typing was read and moved nothing on screen. Shift + Q flips it from the dashboard itself, with a message saying which way it landed, for the times you want the other mode for one search.

A search that finds nothing says where to look. Typing a bookmark's name into the overlay reported nothing found while the bookmark sat on the page behind it — because a plain query looks for a shortcut, not a name. When there is nothing by that shortcut but something by that name, the overlay now says so in one line, with how many there are, and Enter runs the search the other way. When nothing matches either, “nothing found” stays the answer.

A search you arrive with is searched by name. A query from the address bar, a deep link, or a link someone sent you was matched against shortcuts only, so a full bookmark name found nothing and the overlay opened on a query you could not revise.
A round of checks keeps its place. Checking a page of bookmarks wrote each result on its own, and a round interrupted halfway left the report describing a mix of two runs.
